title: Area and perimeter
lede: Perimeter is the fence; area is the grass. Learn the core formulas and the trick for odd shapes.

sections.md:
## Two different questions
- **Perimeter** is the distance **around** a shape. Add up the side lengths. Units: feet, meters.
- **Area** is the space **inside**. Units are squared: ft², m², because you're counting unit squares.

## The formulas
| Shape | Area |
|---|---|
| Rectangle | length × width |
| Square | side² |
| Parallelogram | base × height |
| Triangle | ½ × base × height |
| Trapezoid | ½ × (base₁ + base₂) × height |

The **height** is always measured **straight up** (perpendicular to the base), not along a slanted side.

## Why the triangle is half
Any triangle is exactly half of a parallelogram with the same base and height. Copy it, flip the copy, and the two fit together. That's where the ½ comes from.

## Odd shapes: split or subtract
For an L-shape or a room with a cutout, either **split** it into rectangles and add the areas, or draw the big rectangle around it and **subtract** the missing piece.

sections.title: Composite shape
sections.problem: An L-shaped floor: a 12 ft × 10 ft rectangle with a 4 ft × 5 ft corner cut out. Find the area.

sections.title: Scaling trap
sections.problem: You double every side of a square. What happens to the area?
steps: A side of s has area s².
sections.answer: The area becomes **4 times** bigger, not 2 times.

sections.label: Remember
sections.md: When you scale a shape by a factor k, perimeter scales by k but area scales by **k²**. This is why a 16-inch pizza has about 1.8 times the pizza of a 12-inch one.

practice.q: A rectangle is 9 m by 6 m. What is its perimeter?
Find the area of a triangle with base 10 and height 7.
A trapezoid has bases 8 and 12 and height 5. Area?
A parallelogram has base 11 cm and height 4 cm. Its slanted side is 5 cm. Area?
practice.why: Base × height. The slanted side is a distractor.
